I am Dr. Agent. To begin our evaluation, can you tell me if you or your family have a history of easy bruising or bleeding that stops slowly?

REQUEST TEST: PT_and_PTT

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Complete Blood Count shows Platelets at 280,000 /μL (normal), Prothrombin Time (PT) is 12 seconds (normal), and Partial Thromboplastin Time (aPTT) is 30 seconds (normal). Despite normal counts and coagulation times, the Special Test (ELISA Binding Assay) reveals that platelet surfaces are deficient in GIIb/IIIa receptors, which correlates with the observed diffuse petechiae and gum bleeding.

speaker: Patient
text: 4-year-old male. The child's parent reports that the child has been experiencing frequent episodes of nosebleeds and has had several instances of bleeding from the gums. Additionally, there have been occurrences of unexplained bruising and petechiae, primarily on the distal extremities.

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Frequent epistaxis. I also have Mucous membrane bleeding, Diffuse petechiae on distal extremities. To keep my notes clear, please give only one final answer and keep it to a single direct conclusion.
